## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR deletes `app/defaults.json`, but `app/startup.py` still loads that file, so `load_defaults()` now crashes. That is a critical defect and needs fixing before merge. Two important defects should also be fixed: `is_valid_port` rejects port 65535, and `load_config` silently returns `{}` on every error. The suggestions below are smaller: a `normalize_host` docstring that contradicts the code, and an untested trailing-dot branch.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Any call to `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError`, because this PR deletes `app/defaults.json` while the untouched `app/startup.py:6` still reads it with `Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text()`. The base commit that added the file is titled "test: add required application defaults", and nothing in the diff replaces the file or updates `startup.py`. Restore `app/defaults.json`, or change `load_defaults()` in the same PR to get its defaults from somewhere else (for example an in-code `{"timeout": 30}`). — Any code path that calls `load_defaults()` fails at runtime, so loading application defaults breaks after merge.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False`, but the docstring says "True when p is a usable TCP port (1-65535)", because the check is `0 < p < 65535` and leaves out the upper bound. The added `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound` only checks 0, 1 and 8080, so the upper boundary is never tested. Change the condition to `0 < p <= 65535` and add assertions that 65535 is valid and 65536 is not. — Configurations that use port 65535 are wrongly rejected, and no test protects the upper bound.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — A missing config file, an unreadable file, or malformed JSON all make `load_config` return `{}`, because `except Exception: return {}` swallows `FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError` and JSON decode errors without logging anything or telling the caller. Neither the docstring ("Load the JSON config at path.") nor a nearby comment says this fallback is intentional or describes what the caller sees, so a mistyped path looks the same as an empty config. Either catch only `FileNotFoundError` (if a missing file really should mean an empty config), document that, and let decode and permission errors propagate, or log the path and exception before returning the default. — Operators who mistype a config path or ship broken JSON get the application running on empty settings with no error to diagnose.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — For `normalize_host("")` the docstring says the function "returns None when h is empty", but the code returns `""` (`if h == "": return ""` at line 36–37). A caller that follows the docstring with `if normalize_host(h) is None:` will never detect empty input. Decide which return value is intended, then make the code and docstring agree and add a test for the empty case. — Callers that rely on the documented `None` will treat empty hosts as valid.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — No test exercises the trailing-dot branch of `normalize_host` (input `"Example.COM."` should return `"example.com"`). The only added test, `test_normalize_host_lowercases`, passes `"Example.COM"`, which has no trailing dot, so lines 40–41 never run. Add an assertion such as `normalize_host("Example.COM.") == "example.com"`. — A regression in the stripping of fully qualified dots would go unnoticed.

## Strengths
- The new `ms` branch in `parse_timeout` has a direct test (`parse_timeout("1500ms") == 1.5`) that would fail if the suffix were handled wrongly.
- The lower port boundary is pinned on both sides (0 invalid, 1 valid) in `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound`.
